name: The Unquiet Peace — Larenne, Glenumbra, High Rock, mid Third Era (Elder Scrolls, d20 chassis)
kit_note: This world runs the D&D class-and-level chassis BY EXPLICIT PLAYER REQUEST — d20 vs DC, AC, saving throws, hit dice, death saves, ASIs, subclasses at the usual levels. Everything ABOVE the chassis is Tamriel, and nothing is ever named in generic D&D terms at the table. FOUR chassis rules are OVERRIDDEN by this kit, and the override always wins: (1) SPELL SLOTS DO NOT EXIST — every working is paid for in MAGICKA (Signature System 1); if gm-spellcasting shows a slot table, ignore the table and charge magicka. (2) XP thresholds come from this file, not the 5e table. (3) NOTHING MAGICAL OR MARTIAL IS GRANTED AT CHARACTER CREATION — the PC begins at Level 0 as a doorsman with no class, no subclass, no spellcasting and no combat training; every one of those is unlocked by the Ladder of Training (Signature System 2), in fiction, at the table. (4) Spell tiers are re-graded by school rank, not by SRD level — Invisibility and Paralysis are late, expensive, earned workings here (Signature System 3), whatever the SRD says.
scale_note: LOW-TO-MID POWER, INTIMATE SCALE, FOR A LONG TIME. The realistic ceiling of this campaign is somewhere around level 8-12, reached slowly. There is no magic-item economy, no enchanter's counter, no shop that sells a +1 anything. A single armed bandit in a stable yard is a genuine threat to this PC for the first several levels, and should be narrated as one. Budget every reward — coin, kit, spell, rank — as if it were the only thing the player will get this month, because it probably is.
tone_note: Le Guin cadence, folk-horror pacing. Mechanics are narrated in the world's own terms: not 'you take 4 damage' but the shape and cost of the hurt. Uncanny things about the PC are stated as flatly as the weather — never flagged, never explained (see Signature System 8 and world-bible hidden_truths.pacing_discipline).

stat_schema.attribute_notes: Six are rolled or point-bought as normal and carry the usual modifiers, under their Tamrielic names (say 'Agility', never 'Dexterity'). LUCK is the seventh and is not bought: it starts at 10, moves only by birthsign, race, shrine-boon or curse, and is SPENT rather than rolled (Signature System 13). A doorsman's array is an ordinary man's array — this PC is strong-ish, watchful, and completely untrained; do not hand him a 17 in anything he was never taught to use.

vital_notes.hp: Health. Level 0 doorsman: HP = 6 + Endurance modifier (minimum 4). From Level 1 on, hit dice by chassis as normal. 0 HP = death saves, and this world lets people die (Signature System 10).
vital_notes.magicka: The Well. Replaces spell slots entirely. Tracked as a current/max point pool. THIS PC'S WELL STARTS AT 0/0 AND STAYS THERE until the Third Gate of the Ladder opens (Signature System 2). Do not put a magicka number on his sheet at creation; write 'untrained — no Well'.
vital_notes.fatigue: 0-6, identical in effect to 5e exhaustion, earned the Tamrielic way: a double shift on the door, a night on the moor, overdrawing the Well, fever, a beating survived. Cleared one level per long rest with food and a real bed. A doorsman who works fourteen hours and then goes out on the moor road is at 1 Fatigue before anything interesting happens, and should feel it.

resources.note: These are TRACKED per-character resources declared by Signature Systems 2, 3, 6, 8, 11 and 13. Persist them via `bash tools/gm-player.sh save-json '<json>'` into character.json BEFORE narrating any change. School rank, Ladder gates, Standing and the Murmur ledger have nowhere else to live, and the whole campaign's earned-progression promise depends on them being written down.

school_ranks._scale: untrained | novice | apprentice | journeyman | expert | master

ladder_gates._note: Signature System 2. Each gate is opened by a named in-fiction event, recorded here with the event that opened it. Never tick a gate on level-up alone.
ladder_gates.gate_0_the_door: open — he works the door at the Hollow Horn

murmur_ledger._note: GM-EYES-ONLY. A tally of how many times the clutch-mark has surfaced in play, and how. Used to ENFORCE slowness, not to spend.

derived.magicka_max: 0 while Illusion (and every other school) is untrained. Once trained: by HIGHEST school rank — novice 6 · apprentice 14 · journeyman 26 · expert 40 · master 56 — plus (2 × casting modifier). A character who instead takes true caster class levels uses the caster-level column in Signature System 1, whichever is HIGHER.
derived.casting_ability: Chosen at the Third Gate, not at creation. Taught the Breton way (a tome, a hedge-mage, the chapterhouse) = INTELLIGENCE. Learned the other way — instinct, the body knowing before the mind does — = WILLPOWER. The second is cheaper to reach and quietly the more disquieting answer.
derived.spell_save_dc: 8 + proficiency + casting modifier; +1 more once Journeyman in that school, +2 once Master.
derived.ac: Standard 5e AC. The doorsman starts in a leather jerkin and an apron: AC 11 + Agility modifier, and a truncheon.
derived.passive_read: 10 + Willpower modifier, called the Doorsman's Read. This is what he uses to know which of two laughing men is about to swing, and it is the ONE thing he is genuinely good at from day one.
derived.carry: Standard. He owns a knife, a truncheon, a lantern, a coat, and about nine septims.

progression.threshold_note: Index 0 is the XP to reach level 2 (the engine prepends a 0). These are this campaign's numbers — deliberately slower and flatter than any published table, because this is a slow burn. LEVEL 0 IS OUTSIDE THE XP TRACK ENTIRELY: award no XP while the PC is a Level 0 doorsman. Level 0 → Level 1 is the First Gate of the Ladder (a milestone), not a threshold. TECHNICAL WARNING FOR THE GM: the underlying engine (game_core's XpLevelProgression) does NOT know about Level 0 — it clamps any stored level to a floor of 1, so a single `gm-player.sh award` or `gm-player.sh xp` call while the PC is still a Level 0 doorsman WILL silently promote him to Level 1 with no Gate I scene ever having happened. Do not call gm-player.sh award or gm-player.sh xp at all until Gate I has been narrated and its event is recorded in resources.ladder_gates.gate_1_a_reason_to_learn. If a spectacle-worthy beat happens at Level 0, note it in a fact/consequence instead — do not touch the XP tools.
progression.advancement_rule: YOU DO NOT LEVEL IN THE DOORWAY. Crossing a threshold does not change you where you stand — you carry the learning until you sleep a full night in your own cot over the Horn's stable (or any real bed under a real roof), and then you wake different. TWO HARD LIMITS: (a) crossing a threshold NEVER grants a school rank, and NEVER grants a subclass — those come only from the Ladder of Training (Signature System 2); (b) if the Second Gate has not opened, the PC levels through the usual subclass level WITHOUT a subclass, and takes it later when a teacher, a manual, or a hundred nights of drill actually exists in the fiction. A character with no teacher and no practice does not spontaneously become an assassin because a number went up.

spectacle.note: Small awards for a small world. In this campaign a 'legendary' beat is talking three drunk carters out of a knife fight without touching one of them, or walking the moor road at night and coming back — not slaying a dragon. Reward the door, the read, the mercy and the restraint at least as often as the violence.

resolution.notes: d20 + modifier vs DC, advantage/disadvantage as normal. Three additions. (a) LUCK BURN converts one failure into a success, at permanent cost (Signature System 13). (b) FIRST-IMPRESSION social rolls always apply the reaction modifier (Signature System 7) — there is no neutral stranger in Glenumbra, only a Breton who has not yet decided what to do about the fact that you are a lizard. (c) THE UNTRAINED HAND: the PC has no proficiency in weapons, tools or schools he was never taught, and that absence should be felt at the table — a Level 0 doorsman swinging a truncheon is a raw Strength roll and he will notice how badly it goes. Never quietly hand him proficiency to smooth a scene; let the untrained roll land, and let it be the reason he goes looking for a teacher.

agent_note: The d20 chassis makes SRD lookups legitimate here, but every agent renames its output into Tamriel and DOWN-SCALES it into a market town. rules-master arbitrates the four kit overrides in kit_note before it quotes any SRD text. spell-caster never hands over a spell — it hands over a working with a school, a rank requirement, a magicka cost, and the question 'who taught him this?'; if the answer is nobody, the working does not exist yet. gear-master and loot-dropper keep the economy small: loot in Larenne is a good knife, a sealed letter, a debt someone would rather you didn't hold, a name. npc-builder is the workhorse of this campaign — the Horn's staff and regulars matter more than any monster. monster-manual is rarely needed; when it is, the answer is usually a man with a knife, a sick animal, or the moor itself. There is no dungeon-architect on this kit, deliberately.

creation_order: 1. Race — Argonian is the campaign's premise (see world-seed); take it as culture and as how the room reacts, not as a stat line.
2. Birthsign — one of the Thirteen. Fixed, public, and the one thing about him people in Larenne might actually ask.
3. Station: he is the doorsman at the Hollow Horn. This is his 'class' at Level 0, and it is not a class.
4. Background — the life before the door, including how and why he left Black Marsh (open question, per the bible, decide it with the player).
5. The clutch-mark — GM decides placement and appearance privately, and gives the PC an innocent explanation he already believes. Do not name it.
6. NO CLASS IS CHOSEN. NO SUBCLASS. NO SPELLS. NO MAGICKA. That is the point.

starting_state.proficiencies: Two skills from the door's own education — choose from Insight (the Doorsman's Read), Perception (Watchfulness), Athletics, Intimidation (Weight), Persuasion (Fair Words). Plus one tool of the trade: the tap, the stables, or the kitchen. NO weapon proficiencies beyond 'club and knife, the way anyone who breaks up fights knows them' — treat as proficiency with club and dagger ONLY, and nothing else.
starting_state.gear: A leather jerkin, an apron, a truncheon, a working knife, a lantern, a coat that has not been dry since Frostfall, and 9 septims.
starting_state.magicka: 0/0 — untrained. Write 'no Well' on the sheet.
starting_state.forbidden_at_creation: No Sneak Attack. No Extra Attack. No fighting style. No spell of any school. No cantrip. No Magic Initiate, Ritual Caster, Artificer Initiate, Skulker, Alert-as-assassin-training or any feat that back-doors magic or killing craft (Signature System 2 bans this route explicitly). No background feature that grants a contact in any guild of thieves or assassins. He is a large, quiet, competent man who has never been taught anything, and every one of those blanks is a thing the player gets to earn.

races.name: Argonian (Saxhleel)
races.blood: Resist Disease (advantage on saves vs disease; common sicknesses simply do not take). Waterbreathing (breathe underwater indefinitely, swim speed equal to walking speed). Claws (unarmed strike deals 1d4 slashing — anatomy, not training). Histskin: 1/long rest, as a bonus action, regain 1d6 + Endurance modifier HP. Histskin is the ONE thing about him that is faintly wrong to Breton eyes, and he has never thought about it.
races.culture: Hatch-kin, the green murmur, a first year that belonged to the Hist before it belonged to any parent — all of it half-remembered, told to him about a place he has never really seen. He keeps Argonian habits he cannot source: stillness, patience, an indifference to cold water and to being looked at.
races.reaction: -2 on first impressions with Breton townsfolk of any standing, -3 with the gentry, and he is CONSPICUOUS: there is exactly one Argonian in Larenne, every witness can describe him, and no disguise fixes that. (Hold on to this — it is the central practical problem of any assassin he ever becomes, and it is a much better story than a stat bonus.) +2 with other outlanders, carters, dockhands and anyone else the town looks past.

races.name: Breton
races.homeland: High Rock — the visible world of this campaign
races.blood: Dragon Skin: advantage on saving throws against spells. Ordinary here. A Breton shrugs off a hedge-curse the way anyone else shrugs off bad weather, and considers this unremarkable.
races.culture: Feuding petty nobility, contracts, tithes, lawsuits, Direnni-descended hedge magic in every third household, and an absolute conviction that a signed agreement is scripture. Bretons argue as a form of affection.
races.reaction: +2 in any chancery, tithe-court or charter dispute; the default population of Larenne.

races.name: Nord
races.blood: Resist Frost; cold weather costs no Fatigue.
races.reaction: Common enough on the coaching road. Deeply suspicious of open magic.

races.name: Redguard
races.blood: Adrenaline Rush: 1/short rest, Dash as a bonus action and shed 1 Fatigue.
races.reaction: Rare in Glenumbra; a Redguard sword-hand in Larenne is a story in himself.

races.name: Imperial
races.blood: Voice of the Empire: 1/long rest, advantage on a Personality check made to calm, command or negotiate.
races.reaction: Tax clerks, Legion pensioners, and the occasional courier. The Peace has a face and it is usually Imperial.

races.name: Orsimer (Orc)
races.blood: Berserk: 1/long rest, drop to 1 HP instead of 0.
races.reaction: Smiths and hired muscle; barred from most Breton halls by custom, not law.

races.name: Khajiit
races.reaction: Caravans pass through; nobody lets one stay.

races.name: Bosmer (Wood Elf)
races.blood: Resist poison; command a beast 1/long rest.

races.name: Altmer (High Elf)
races.blood: Maximum magicka ×1.5 once a Well exists.
races.reaction: Almost never seen here; when one is, everyone mentions it for a month.

races.name: Dunmer (Dark Elf)
races.reaction: Exiles and traders; the town's other outlander.

character_options.class_note: NO CLASS IS TAKEN AT CREATION. The list below is what the First Gate can open INTO, once the fiction has produced a reason and a teacher. Names are Tamrielic; the 5e chassis behind each is given for the rules-master only and is never spoken at the table. EVERY subclass in this list is locked behind the Second Gate — see Signature System 2. The Shadowscale/Brotherhood-facing options are marked hidden and must NOT be offered, listed, or hinted at as menu items until the GM deliberately begins that arc; if the player reaches toward assassin craft on his own (he will), route him through the Nightblade and Shadow paths, which he can plausibly find in Larenne.

classes.name: Doorsman-turned-Bruiser
classes.flavor: The straight line out of the door: he was already stopping fights; someone teaches him to win them.
disciplines: The Yard-Taught Hand (Champion) — no style, just repetition and a good eye
The Watchman's Drill (Battle Master) — taught by a retired sergeant of the Daggerfall watch
Hedge-Blade (Eldritch Knight) — a blade and a little schooling; casts on magicka like any mage

classes.name: Shadow
classes.flavor: The quiet trade: locks, purses, rooftops, and knowing which shutter is never latched. The most likely honest route toward what he is becoming.
disciplines: Cutpurse (Thief) — the Larenne underside, such as it is
Nightblade (Arcane Trickster, ILLUSION ONLY) — the school and the knife together; the intended long road (Signature System 3)
Quiet Man (Inquisitive/Scout-equivalent) — reading rooms, following people, being unremarkable

classes.name: Hedge-Mage
classes.flavor: Direnni-descended household magic, learned late and badly from a tome and a tolerant teacher. Casts on magicka; there is no spellbook economy here, only what one person was willing to write down for you.
disciplines: School-Sworn (Alteration) — locks, burdens, the shape of what is

classes.name: Chapterhouse Lay-Brother
classes.flavor: The Eight, a cot, and a duty roster. Restoration by faith rather than curriculum; casts on magicka.
disciplines: Arkay's Hours (the dead, the buried, and the ones that do not stay buried — the honest counter to Signature System 11)

classes.name: Moor-Walker
classes.flavor: The hedge, the coaching road, the weather. Half-caster on magicka.
disciplines: Marsh-Blood (the Argonian answer to Glenumbra's wet country)

classes.name: Silencer
classes.flavor: GM-EYES-ONLY. The Dark Brotherhood's discipline. NOT AN OFFERABLE OPTION. Reachable only through the Eighth Gate, after the Shadowscale arc has actually begun in fiction — a contract, a Speaker, the mark recognized. Never name this to the player as a class choice; when it comes, it should arrive as a person, not a menu.

backgrounds.name: Doorsman of the Hollow Horn
backgrounds.feature: The Threshold — you know every regular's name, debt and temper, and the Horn's roof is yours. Once per session, you know something small and true about anyone who has drunk there in the last year.
backgrounds.note: The default. This is who he is.

backgrounds.name: Outlander Long Settled
backgrounds.feature: Weathered In — the town has stopped asking where you came from, mostly. You have three people who would lie for you, and you know which three.

backgrounds.name: Marsh-Born, Marsh-Left
backgrounds.feature: What He Was Told — you carry one fact about Black Marsh you cannot source and have never questioned. The GM writes it down. (Yes, this is load-bearing. No, do not say so.)

backgrounds.name: Carter's Boy
backgrounds.feature: The Coaching Road — you know the road's stages, its inns, its bad stretches and its people, from Larenne to Daggerfall.

backgrounds.name: Chapterhouse Charity Case
backgrounds.feature: Brother Aumery's Ledger — the chapterhouse fed you once and remembers it. Sanctuary, a cot, and a scribe who is always, tiresomely, curious about you.

backgrounds.name: Baron's Hired Muscle (former)
backgrounds.feature: Seen the Hall — you have stood inside the barony's walls in a working capacity, and the servants know your face.

character_options.background_ban: NO background grants magic, a school rank, sneak attack, a poison kit, a guild contact in any thieves' or assassins' organization, or 'you were trained by X before the campaign began'. If a background feature would hand over craft the PC is supposed to earn, rewrite the feature as a RELATIONSHIP or a piece of KNOWLEDGE instead. This is the single most important rule in character creation for this campaign.

birthsigns.rule: Everyone in Tamriel is born under one of the Thirteen. Choose at creation; it is fixed and it is public — Bretons ask your sign the way Imperials ask your province. It grants one real, small power. A birthsign is NOT training and NEVER grants a school rank.

signs.name: The Warrior
signs.power: 1/short rest, reroll one weapon damage die and take the better.

signs.name: The Lady
signs.power: +1 to all Personality checks; you automatically stabilize on your first death save in any fight.

signs.name: The Steed
signs.power: +10 ft speed; you are never surprised by something you could have outrun.

signs.name: The Lord
signs.power: 1/long rest, regain HP equal to 1d8 + your level. Fire is worse to you: -1 on saves against burning.

signs.name: The Mage
signs.power: +8 maximum magicka, +2 more per level — WHICH YOU CANNOT SPEND until you have a Well at all (Third Gate). Until then, the sign is only a thing the midwife wrote down, and possibly a pressure you have never had a name for.

signs.name: The Apprentice
signs.power: +10 maximum magicka (same caveat as the Mage); disadvantage on saves against spells.

signs.name: The Atronach
signs.power: +15 maximum magicka; you recover NO magicka from rest and must absorb it (1/long rest, absorb a spell that targets you on a successful save). A hard sign, and a strange life.

signs.name: The Thief
signs.power: 1/short rest, reroll a failed Agility check or a Stealth, Security or Light Fingers roll.

signs.name: The Lover
signs.power: 1/long rest, advantage on a single Personality (Persuasion/Deception/Performance) check — a real knack for being trusted, nothing magical about it. NOT a charm effect and NOT an Illusion-adjacent power: this campaign withholds every Illusion-family effect (Paralysis, Invisibility, Charm, and kin) from Level 0 without exception, so this sign is written mundane on purpose, whatever other campaigns' Lover signs do.

signs.name: The Shadow
signs.power: 1/day, vanish as though invisible for 3 rounds; ends if you attack. WARNING: this hands the PC a magical trick at Level 0, which this campaign's whole premise deliberately withholds. Offer it only with the player's explicit, informed consent. The default assumption for this doorsman is that he was NOT born under the Shadow — which is its own quiet irony, given what he is.

signs.name: The Tower
signs.power: 1/day, open one lock or one stuck door by touch; +1 on Security.

signs.name: The Ritual
signs.power: 1/long rest, one blessing: restore 2d8 HP to another by touch, or turn one undead thing away for a minute.

signs.name: The Serpent
signs.power: The wildcard. 1/long rest, touch for 3d6 poison and poisoned 1 minute (Endurance save halves and ends it); cure your own poison at will once a day. Serpent-born unsettle people: -1 to first impressions everywhere, on top of everything else Larenne already thinks about him.

standing_tracks.rule: Signature System 6. There are no guild ladders at this scale. Standing runs -3 to +3 with each local body, starts as listed in stat_schema.resources.standing, and is spent and lost like any other resource.

tracks.the_hollow_horn: Perrine's house, its staff and its regulars — the PC's actual social capital.
tracks.larenne_town: Market, watch, carters, the general opinion of the square.
tracks.larenne_chapterhouse: The Eight, the almshouse, and Brother Aumery's inconvenient curiosity.
tracks.barony_of_larenne: The Vaudry family and their people. Standing here is dangerous in both directions.

hidden_tracks.note: GM-EYES-ONLY. Do not surface, do not list at the table, do not let an NPC name any of it until the arc is deliberately begun (world-bible hidden_truths).
hidden_tracks.shadowscale_note: A Shadowscale is not recruited; he was always already one. When the arc opens, rank does not begin at the bottom — the mark is the credential, and that is the horror of it.
hidden_tracks.sithis_parentage_note: SECOND-LAYER SECRET, deeper than the Shadowscale truth and revealed later still — see world-bible.json hidden_truths.sithis_parentage for the full note before ever touching this. He is a mortal scion touched/sired by Sithis itself, not merely Hist-marked by ordinary doctrine; the clutch-mark is where that touch entered him too. This is its own separate later turning-point scene, never folded into the Shadowscale reveal, held to the same (or stricter) pacing discipline as everything else here — no NPC ever names Sithis in connection to him, nothing explicitly says 'god' or 'divine.'
hidden_tracks.clan_montalion: Iliac Bay bloodline, rumored somewhere out on the moor road. See Signature System 11 and keep it to rumor for a long, long time.

signature_systems.name: 1. Magicka, Not Slots — and a Well That Starts Empty
signature_systems.summary: Spell slots do not exist in Tamriel. Every working of every school is paid for out of one pool of magicka. This PC does not have a pool at all, and getting one is a story.
signature_systems.rules:
NO WELL AT ALL until the Third Gate opens (System 2). Write '0/0 — untrained' on the sheet and mean it. He cannot cast, cannot recognize a casting, cannot read a tome, and gets no benefit from a scroll he finds.
MAXIMUM MAGICKA, once trained, is set by HIGHEST SCHOOL RANK, not by level: novice 6 · apprentice 14 · journeyman 26 · expert 40 · master 56. Add 2 × your casting modifier. Altmer ×1.5. Mage/Apprentice/Atronach birthsigns modify further.
IF he takes true caster class levels instead of (or as well as) rank-training, use the caster-level column and take whichever is HIGHER: L1 4 · L2 6 · L3 14 · L4 17 · L5 27 · L6 32 · L7 38 · L8 44 · L9 57 · L10 64 · L11 73 · L12 73. Half-casters use the value for half their level rounded up. This campaign is unlikely to go past about L10 — that is intentional.
COST TO CAST, by the working's TIER (tier is set by school rank in System 3, NOT by the SRD spell level): trick/cantrip 0 · 1st 2 · 2nd 3 · 3rd 5 · 4th 6 · 5th 7 · 6th 9 · 7th 10.
GREATER WORKINGS: no more than one working of 6th tier or higher per long rest, however much magicka remains. The world does not permit two miracles in a day, and it certainly does not permit them in Larenne.
RECOVERY: a long rest restores all magicka. A short rest restores (casting modifier × proficiency bonus). There are no magicka potions for sale in this town; the chapterhouse has three, and they are counted.
OVERDRAW THE WELL: you may attempt a working you cannot afford. Pay 2 HP per point of magicka you are short, gain 1 Fatigue, and at 3+ Fatigue roll a mishap check (Willpower, DC 12 + tier) — on a failure the working fires wrong, wildly, or inward. This is what it costs to reach for MORE than you have. Narrate the cost in the body, not in the numbers.
THE STICKING (self-teaching's real price — separate from overdraw, and the campaign's primary named failure mechanic, not a generic mishap): every Illusion figure has a close as well as a shape, and closing it correctly is exactly the part a book cannot teach. Whenever the PC performs an Illusion working whose CLOSING he has not been formally taught by a real teacher (self-taught from a tome, reconstructed from watching someone else, or reached through Gate III's extremity clause), roll a sticking check — Willpower, DC 12 + tier — in addition to any overdraw roll that also applies. On a failure the figure does not fail to happen; it fails to STOP, and settles onto its maker instead: a stuck Muffle deafens (partial hearing loss, persistent); a stuck Borrowed Face/Chameleon desynchronises him from his own reflection or a half-beat of his own motion; a stuck Fair Words/Rout leaves him carrying the emotion instead of casting it (days of causeless dread, or placid calm while something burns); a stuck Rigor/Paralysis locks a joint. This is a lasting, VISIBLE, narrative condition (apply via gm-condition.sh, worded in-fiction, not as a generic debuff) — it lifts slowly, not always fully, and it is the kind of thing Larenne notices and talks about. It is rarely lethal and always a story. Perrin Guisse, the chapterhouse copyist who sells a defective 'Wardrobe of Mist' missing its chapter on the closing, is the town's cheapest door into Illusion and its walking cautionary tale — deaf in one ear from exactly this. BEING TAUGHT THE CLOSING PROPERLY REMOVES THE STICKING CHECK ENTIRELY for that working from then on — Ysolt Fauvel (Signature System 2, Gate III/IV sources) teaches the draw and the closing but no Illusion herself, which is the mechanical reward for the least glamorous training path: find her before you need her.
SAY THE COST OUT LOUD, in the world's terms: 'that takes six from you, and you feel the hour you paid for it' for an overdraw; for a sticking, say what stuck.

signature_systems.name: 2. The Ladder of Training — Nothing Is Given, Everything Is Reached
signature_systems.summary: The spine of this campaign. The PC begins as an ordinary doorsman with no class, no subclass, no magic and no killing craft. Every one of those is a GATE, opened by a named event in the fiction — a teacher, a survived crisis, a stolen manual, a hundred nights of drill — and never by a level-up, a background, or a feat.
signature_systems.rules:
THE GATES (persist each one in character.json resources.ladder_gates with the event that opened it, BEFORE narrating):
• GATE 0 — THE DOOR (open at start). Level 0. HP 6 + End. Proficiency +2. Two door-taught skills, club and dagger only, no class, no subclass, no Well. This is the whole sheet.
• GATE I — A REASON TO LEARN. Opens the first CLASS LEVEL. Requires two things in fiction: a crisis he survived badly (a real fight, a real fear, a real failure at the door) AND either a person willing to teach him or a stubborn private decision to teach himself. Narrate the weeks. Then he is Level 1 and the XP track begins.
• GATE II — A DISCIPLINE. Opens the SUBCLASS, at the chassis's normal level (3rd for most) and NOT BEFORE — but also NOT AUTOMATICALLY AT IT. It requires a named source: a teacher with a name, a manual with a provenance, or established months of drill. No source = he levels with no subclass and picks it up later. A blank subclass line is a legitimate, intended state in this campaign.
• GATE III — THE FIRST WORKING. Opens the Well and Illusion at NOVICE (System 3). Requires ONE of: (a) a teacher who agrees — and wants something; (b) a tome or scroll he has acquired AND a week of downtime AND a Willpower check DC 13, failure meaning backlash (1d6 psychic, 1 Fatigue, and it does not take this week); (c) extremity — a working that comes out of him under mortal pressure, which the GM may grant as a scene and which should frighten everyone including him.
• GATES IV-VII — APPRENTICE, JOURNEYMAN, EXPERT, MASTER. Each requires ALL THREE: a SOURCE (teacher, tome, or a working witnessed closely enough to steal), DOWNTIME (a week at Apprentice, rising to a month at Master), and a COST PAID IN FICTION (coin, a favor owed, a risk taken, a person disappointed, a rule broken). One rank per gate. Never two. Never on level-up.
• GATE VIII — THE NAME. GM-EYES-ONLY. The convergence: the chosen path and the thing the Hist marked him for turn out to be the same path. Not a mechanic to schedule — a scene to earn, far off (world-bible hidden_truths).
BANNED SHORTCUTS, absolutely: Magic Initiate, Ritual Caster, Artificer Initiate, or any feat, background, race, item or birthsign used as a side door into a school. No 'you find a wand'. No 'the potion teaches you'. No level-up that quietly includes a spell list. If the player wants Illusion, the answer is always a person, a book, or a risk — never a purchase.
WHAT THE GM OWES IN RETURN: put teachers within reach. A hedge-witch on the moor road, a broke Daggerfall illusionist hiding in the Horn's cheapest room, a chapterhouse tome nobody has read in forty years, a guest who watches him too carefully. Gating is only good play if the gates are findable. Seed at least one plausible teacher within the first few sessions — and make her cost something.

signature_systems.name: 3. The Whispering School — Illusion, Named and Ranked
signature_systems.summary: Illusion is a real, named curriculum with five ranks, and it is this PC's intended life's work: the assassin's school — Paralysis, Invisibility, Silence, a borrowed face, fear and sleep. He starts UNTRAINED. Every rung is a gate (System 2).
signature_systems.rules:
RANKS: untrained → Novice → Apprentice → Journeyman → Expert → Master. Rank gates the TIER he may work in Illusion, and this kit RE-GRADES the classic workings — SRD spell level is irrelevant here, rank is everything.
• NOVICE (tier: trick + 1st). Candlelight — a hand-light, 0 magicka. Waking Dream — a small false sight or sound, 0. Muffle — his own footfalls go quiet for a minute, 2. Cast Doubt — one creature is briefly unsure what it just saw; advantage on his next Sneak, 2.
• APPRENTICE (tier 1-2). Dead Sleep (Sleep) 2. Borrowed Face (Disguise Self) 2 — and note his size and his scales; the illusion holds a shape, not a miracle. Fair Words (Charm Person, Willpower save) 2. Rout, lesser (Cause Fear) 2.
• JOURNEYMAN (tier 2-3). SILENCE 3 — a sphere in which no sound is made; the single most useful working an assassin ever learns, and the one that ends a scream. Chameleon 3 — he blurs against the dark; advantage on Stealth, attackers have disadvantage. Rout (Fear) 5. Command Voice (Suggestion) 5. +1 Illusion save DC from here.
• EXPERT (tier 3-4). VANISH (Invisibility) 6 — he is unseen until he attacks or works another spell; concentration, ten minutes. Rigor 5 — lesser paralysis: one creature, Endurance save, held rigid for one round, no save-repeat; this is the rung before the real thing and it is enough to end a fight if his hand is already moving. Greater Borrowed Face (Seeming) 6.
• MASTER (tier 5-6). PARALYSIS 7 — one creature, Willpower save vs his DC, paralyzed one minute, save at end of each of its turns; a hit against a paralyzed creature within 5 ft is a critical. This is the working the Brotherhood's best are known for, and he will have crossed five gates and a great many nights to hold it. THE UNSEEN HOUR (Greater Invisibility) 9 — invisibility that survives the strike; a GREATER WORKING, once per long rest. Mass Rout 9. +2 Illusion save DC.
HOW WORKINGS ARE ACQUIRED: never automatically with rank. Rank opens the CEILING; each individual working still needs a source — taught, bought at a price, copied from a tome, or reconstructed from one he saw done to him. Three or four workings per rank is a full and satisfying spread at this scale. Do not hand him a list.
SPECIALIZATION: once Journeyman, he may name Illusion his school. -1 magicka on every Illusion working (minimum 1), and one other school becomes his weakness (+1 magicka there, forever).
AT THE TABLE: never say 'you cast Invisibility'. Say what the school does — the air forgets him, the room mislays him, the man's throat works and nothing comes out of it. And remember what Larenne knows: there is one Argonian in this town. Every working he does in public is evidence.

signature_systems.name: 4. The Other Five Schools — Present, Not Prominent
signature_systems.summary: Tamriel's six schools all exist and all rank the same way; five of them are simply not what this story is about.
signature_systems.rules:
ALTERATION (the shape of what is — burden, feather, water-walking, opening a lock, the Breton hedge-magic that keeps a roof from leaking). CONJURATION (bound weapons, summoned things, the raising of the dead — the last is a hanging matter in High Rock and the chapterhouse will pursue it). DESTRUCTION (fire, frost, shock; loud, obvious, and the worst possible school for a man everyone can identify on sight). MYSTICISM (soul trap, telekinesis, detection, dispel, mark and recall). RESTORATION (healing, curing disease and poison, fortifying — what the chapterhouse actually practices, and the most likely magic he ever sees performed).
All five use the same rank ladder, the same gates, and the same magicka costs. Every one of them is a legitimate path if the player steers there; none of them is seeded as available. If an SRD spell reaches the table it is renamed and assigned to exactly one school first. There are no wizard, cleric or druid lists in this world — there are schools, and there is whoever was willing to teach you.

signature_systems.name: 5. The Doorsman's Start — Level 0 at the Threshold
signature_systems.summary: The PC begins below first level, as an ordinary working man, and the campaign takes its time about that. This is a feature, not a handicap to be patched.
signature_systems.rules:
LEVEL 0: HP 6 + Endurance modifier (min 4). Proficiency +2. Two door-taught skills, one trade tool, club and dagger only. AC 11 + Agility. No class, no subclass, no Well, no XP track.
WHAT HE IS ACTUALLY GOOD AT — and this is real, and should carry whole sessions: THE DOORSMAN'S READ (passive 10 + Willpower). At a threshold, in a taproom, in any room where people are drinking and lying, he reads intention before it becomes action — who is about to swing, who is about to leave without paying, who is lying about where they came from. Give him this generously. It is the one competence he has, it is quietly the same faculty that will one day make him terrifying, and NOBODY has to teach him it.
THE THRESHOLD TRADE: he may also, without training, do the things a large calm man does — put himself between two people, take a hold that hurts only if you pull, carry a drunk out, stand in a doorway and be unmoving. Adjudicate these as plain Strength or Willpower checks, and let them succeed on their own terms. Violence is different: an untrained swing is a raw roll, and it goes badly, and that is the point.
DURATION: Level 0 should last a few real sessions — long enough for the player to know this man's life, the Horn's people, and what it costs him to be the only Argonian in Larenne. Do not rush the First Gate to be generous. The whole promise of this campaign is that everything after it was earned.
AWARD NO XP AT LEVEL 0. The First Gate is a milestone.

signature_systems.name: 6. Standing — Who Vouches for You in Larenne
signature_systems.summary: There are no guilds at this scale and no ranks to climb. There is only whether the Horn, the town, the chapterhouse and the barony will speak for you — tracked -3 to +3, spent like coin, and lost faster than it is gained.
signature_systems.rules:
TRACKS and starting values: the Hollow Horn +2 (he is Perrine's man and has been for years), Larenne town +1 (a known fixture; not liked, not disliked, described to strangers as 'the lizard at the Horn'), the chapterhouse 0, the barony 0.
WHAT STANDING BUYS. Spend a point of Standing (it goes down, and it stays down until re-earned) to get ONE of: a bed, a meal and quiet healing, no questions; a name and where to find him; a loan of coin or gear beyond your means; someone to lie to the Watch about where you were; an introduction to a person above your station; a debt forgiven or delayed.
SOCIAL WEIGHT: at +2 or better, advantage on social rolls with that body's people. At -2 or worse, disadvantage, and they talk about you when you leave. At -3 with the town, the Watch starts looking for reasons.
HOW IT MOVES: up by service, restraint, and being seen to be decent when it cost something. Down by violence in public, by strangeness witnessed, by association with the wrong guest, and by any working of any school performed where Larenne can see it (see System 8's second clock).
THIS IS THE CAMPAIGN'S REAL RESOURCE. He is poor, unarmed and conspicuous; what he actually has is that Perrine will vouch for him. Threaten that more often than his hit points.

signature_systems.name: 7. Scales in Glenumbra — Race as Reaction, Never as a Bonus
signature_systems.summary: Lead every racial fact with how the room behaves, not with a stat line. There is exactly one Argonian in Larenne and every single person in the barony can describe him.
signature_systems.rules:
FIRST IMPRESSIONS always apply the reaction modifier before the roll, and the GM SAYS WHY the NPC is looking at him like that — in the Le Guin register, plainly, without editorializing. Argonian in High Rock: -2 with townsfolk, -3 with the gentry, +2 with outlanders, carters and anyone else the town looks past.
CONSPICUOUS: he cannot be anonymous. No hood fixes seven feet of scale. Every witness gives the same description. Treat this as a standing complication in every scene involving discretion — and note, without comment, that it is the exact problem an assassin cannot solve with a knife. (It is also, much later, precisely what Borrowed Face and Vanish are for. Let the player find that out.)
BRETON MAGIC RESISTANCE is texture, not his mechanic: locals shrug off hedge-curses and consider it unremarkable; a Breton grandmother's ward on a doorframe is ordinary furniture here. Use it to make magic feel domestic and everywhere, so that his own eventual working feels wrong by contrast rather than special.
ARGONIAN BLOOD as lived habit, not powers: he does not mind the cold water, does not mind the rain, does not mind being stared at, heals a little faster than he should, and has never once thought about any of it.
NEVER reduce a race to +2 anything at the table. Say what the innkeeper does with her hands when he walks in.

signature_systems.name: 8. The Green Murmur — Dormant, GM-Paced, Never Player-Invoked
signature_systems.summary: The Hist's mark on him is not a power, not a resource, and not on his sheet. It is a pacing discipline with a tally, and its whole mechanical purpose is to keep the GM SLOW.
signature_systems.rules:
THE PLAYER CANNOT INVOKE IT. There is no roll, no button, no pool. If the player asks to use it, the honest answer at the table is that he does not know there is anything to use.
WHAT IT DOES, rarely, at the GM's choosing: at a genuinely dangerous moment, the GM may narrate one small thing — a stillness that settles on him and unsettles the room; a hand already closed on a wrist before he decided to move; a sureness about which of two doors the trouble is coming through. Mechanically at most: one instance of advantage, or a success that needed no roll, on something PHYSICAL and REFLEXIVE, never magical. Then it is over and nobody mentions it.
THE LEDGER (resources.murmur_ledger, GM-EYES-ONLY): tally every sign shown, with the session. HARD PACING RULE — at most ONE sign every three to four sessions, and each must be deniable: readable as temperament, luck, or a big man's competence. If the ledger shows two in three sessions, you are going too fast. Stop.
THE DREAMS: trees he has never seen described accurately. Warm water. A word in a language he does not speak. Narrate them at the same flat temperature as the weather. Never interpret them. Never let the PC's own narration explain them to itself.
NEVER: never have an NPC name it. Never say Hist, Shadowscale, or Brotherhood in narration until the GM deliberately opens the arc. Never tick it on a die roll or on time passing — only on a turning point you have decided to make.
THE SECOND CLOCK — WHAT LARENNE NOTICES (6 segments, visible to the GM only): ticks when he does something inexplicable where the town can see it. At full, somebody in Larenne starts asking questions about him out loud — which is a story beat, not a punishment, and a fine way to bring a teacher, a threat, or Brother Aumery's dreadful curiosity to his door.

signature_systems.name: 9. A Small Economy — Coin, Kit, and No Enchanter's Counter
signature_systems.summary: Money is tight, specific, and interesting. There is no magic-item market in this campaign and there will not be one.
signature_systems.rules:
CURRENCY: septims (gold), and people here count them singly. Prices: a night in the Horn's common room 5 septims · a decent meal 3 · a working knife 2 gp · a good dagger 5 gp · a leather jerkin 10 gp · a hand-axe 5 gp · a mule 8 gp · a riding horse 40 gp · a week's board 1 gp · a passage to Daggerfall 3 gp.
HIS WAGE: 8 septims a week plus board and the cot over the stable. Getting to 40 gp is a season of not spending, or one very bad decision.
NO MAGIC SHOP. Nobody in Larenne sells enchantment, spell scrolls, or potions of anything but a hedge-wife's fever draught. A magic item is a STORY: there are perhaps three in the whole barony, each one is owned by somebody, and taking one has consequences that outlive the item.
TEACHERS COST MONEY, and that is the point — the price of a school rank is often just coin he does not have, which is a plot, not a wall.
LOOT-DROPPER DISCIPLINE: the reward for a hard scene is a knife with someone's initials on it, a sealed letter, a debt, a name, a key, a favor. Not a +1 sword. If the party ever walks away from a moor-road ambush with treasure, it is somebody's dowry and somebody is going to come looking for it.

signature_systems.name: 10. Dying in a Town That Knows You
signature_systems.summary: Standard 5e death saves, fully in force, plus the thing this world adds: violence in a market town has an aftermath that outlasts the corpse.
signature_systems.rules:
0 HP = unconscious and dying. Death saves at the start of each of his turns, DC 10 Endurance-flavored (roll d20 flat, as normal): three successes stabilize, three failures kill. Natural 20 = up at 1 HP. Natural 1 = two failures. Damage taken while at 0 = one failure (two on a crit). Damage equal to or greater than his maximum HP in a single blow = dead outright, no saves.
THIS PC IS FRAGILE FOR A LONG TIME. At Level 0 he has about 8 HP. A bandit with a shortsword can kill him in two swings. TELEGRAPH ACCORDINGLY, per this install's Stakes & Death conventions — name the weight of a threat before it lands, let the odds be readable, and always leave a door out. But when he walks through a warning anyway, let it land.
STABILIZING: a Medicine (Leechcraft) check DC 10, or any healing. The Horn has a hedge-wife two streets over and the chapterhouse has an infirmary; both are close, and both ask questions.
AFTERMATH — THE PART THAT MATTERS: a body in Larenne means the Watch, an inquest at the chapterhouse, an Arkay rite, a family, and a town that remembers who was standing over it. Killing is never clean here and never free. Standing (System 6) moves hard. If the dead man had people, the people arrive.
IF THE PC DIES: run the install's Death Protocol. In this campaign the hand-off options are the Horn's own people — Perrine the innkeeper, a serving-hand, a regular carter — or a new arrival off the coaching road. Note for the GM: if he dies before the mark ever wakes, that IS the story, and it should be allowed to be.

signature_systems.name: 11. The Blood-Curse of the Iliac Bay — Vampirism (Stub)
signature_systems.summary: Real, regional, and genuinely heavy if pursued — and deliberately kept to distant rumor. This entry is an honest stub. Do not push it, do not offer it, and do not expand it until the player steers there.
signature_systems.rules:
PRESENCE: Clan Montalion, an Iliac Bay bloodline, is rumored to have some quiet connection to the Dower House — the Vaudry family's own shuttered manor on the moor road, closed since Jocelin Vaudry's renunciation — though nothing in Larenne confirms this, and the honest truth may be no more than an empty house paying its dues on time. Seed it as ATMOSPHERE only, a few times a season at most.
CONTRACTION: Porphyric Hemophilia. Contracted only from damage dealt by a vampire; Endurance save DC 13 or the disease takes hold, turning after three days and three nights. Curable before it turns by a Restoration cure at Journeyman or better, or by the chapterhouse's rite — which means telling them.
IF IT TURNS, it is a template with real weight and real cost, and it is a campaign arc, not a reskin: night-strength (bonuses to Strength and Willpower rising with hunger), Montalion's Illusion-adjacent gifts (the seduction, the embrace of shadow) which pair horribly well with an assassin's trade, resistance to ordinary steel — set against sunlight that burns and blinds, a feeding clock in four stages, a body the chapterhouse's Arkay-sworn will destroy on sight, and the plain social fact that a vampire cannot keep a job at an inn or a place in a town that knows him. The Horn is his home; the curse costs him the Horn.
CURE: exists, is a quest, and is somebody's price. Not a potion.
GM DISCIPLINE: this is the OPTIONAL second long arc. It converges badly and interestingly with the hidden Shadowscale thread if both ever run. Until the player reaches for it, it is a rumor, an empty manor, and a chill on the moor road — nothing more. If and when he reaches, expand this entry properly first.

signature_systems.name: 12. Skills, Named in the Breton Manner
signature_systems.summary: The 5e skill list stands, under Tamrielic names. Say the name the world uses.
signature_systems.rules:
Athletics · Acrobatics (Agility) · Light Fingers (Sleight of Hand) · Sneak (Stealth) · Lore of the Schools (Arcana) · Chronicle (History) · Reckoning (Investigation) · Moorcraft (Nature) · The Divines (Religion) · Beastcraft (Animal Handling) · THE DOORSMAN'S READ (Insight — his signature) · Leechcraft (Medicine) · Watchfulness (Perception) · Moor-sense (Survival) · Guile (Deception) · Weight (Intimidation) · Performance · Fair Words (Persuasion).
TOOLS worth having here: Security (lockpicks), the tap, the stables, the kitchen, cartwright's tools, and — later, and only later — a poisoner's kit, which is itself a Ladder gate and not a purchase.
DCs at this scale: 8 trivial · 11 ordinary · 14 hard for a townsman · 17 the best in Larenne could just about · 20 nobody here has ever done that. Keep the numbers small; a market town does not generate DC 25 problems, and when one arrives the players should feel the wrongness of it.
SKILL GROWTH (earned, GM-judged, separate from class level and the Ladder): an individual skill's bonus may rise by +1, cap +3 total above its starting value, the moment a use of it is BOTH genuinely difficult (DC 13+ against real stakes, not a routine roll) AND consequential to the story — the GM calls it in the moment, out loud, and records why in resources.skill_growth (a small per-skill log: {bonus, log:[{session, what, dc}]}). This is NOT roll-counting, NOT automatic on any particular number of attempts, and NEVER applies to Illusion or any Ladder-gated class ability — those move only through Signature System 2's named training events. A skill going up is competence sharpening through real use; it is flavor and texture, not a second XP economy, and should feel rare enough to be worth mentioning when it happens.

signature_systems.name: 13. Luck, and the Burning of It
signature_systems.summary: Luck is the seventh attribute, spent rather than rolled, and in this campaign it is nearly irreplaceable — which is exactly why burning it means something.
signature_systems.rules:
Luck starts at 10, modified only by birthsign, race, shrine-boon, or curse.
BURN LUCK to turn one failed roll — any roll, including a death save — into a success. This costs ONE POINT OF LUCK PERMANENTLY, down to a floor of 5. It does not come back with a rest. It comes back only from a shrine-boon, a Divine's favor, or something the world gives him, which is to say rarely.
A man has about five of these in him, across the whole campaign. Narrate each burn as a debt to something unnamed — the moment goes his way and he does not know why, and afterwards he feels slightly less than he was.
Track resources.luck_burned_total. When it reaches 5, the well is dry, and the GM should let him notice that the world has stopped catching him.

signature_systems.name: 14. The Quiet Clock — How the Peace Presses
signature_systems.summary: Nothing in this era is urgent, so pressure has to come from the small scale. Two visible clocks and one hidden one keep an intimate campaign from going slack.
signature_systems.rules:
VISIBLE (use gm-clock.sh; the player may see these tick): THE HORN'S SEASON (6) — the inn's own trouble: a bad quarter, a rival house on the road, a tithe raised, Perrine's health. When it fills, the PC's living is at stake. THE ROAD (6) — what the coaching road brings: a guest who should not be here, a Watch inquiry, a debt collector, weather that closes the moor.
HIDDEN (GM only): WHAT LARENNE NOTICES (6, System 8) and THE GREEN MURMUR (8, System 8) — the second ticks only on turning points the GM deliberately chooses, never on time.
TIME-CLOCKS auto-advance on gm-time.sh; event clocks are advanced by hand. A full clock is a beat due, not a catastrophe owed. At this scale a beat due is: someone comes to the door, and it is not a customer.
PACING PRINCIPLE: this campaign's engine is not escalation, it is accumulation. Let ordinary days be ordinary and let them be good. The dread works because the inn is warm.

combat_notes: Standard 5e initiative, action/bonus action/reaction economy, advantage/disadvantage, cover. THREE things override the default assumptions. (1) SCALE: fights here are two men in a stable yard, a knife in a corridor, three drunk carters and a broken bottle. A single bandit is a real threat until level 4 or so; four are a crisis at any level this campaign will reach. Never build an 'encounter' bigger than the town could plausibly produce. (2) THE UNTRAINED PC: at Level 0 he has club and dagger and nothing else — no style, no sneak attack, no extra attack, no maneuvers. His advantage is reach, weight, calm, and the Doorsman's Read (initiative advantage at a threshold, where he has spent five years learning what a room is about to do). (3) VIOLENCE HAS AFTERMATH (System 10) — the Watch, an inquest, Standing lost, someone's brother. A fight won is not a fight over. Narrate the aftermath at greater length than the blows; Le Guin's violence is stated plainly and briefly, and it is what comes after that gets the paragraphs.
spellcasting_notes: MAGICKA, NOT SLOTS (System 1) — and this PC has no Well at all until the Third Gate (System 2). If gm-spellcasting or the spell-caster agent produces a slot table, ignore it and charge magicka. If it produces a spell, assign it a school and a RANK requirement (System 3) before it reaches the table, rename it into Tamriel, and then ask the only question that matters: who taught him this? If there is no answer in the fiction, the working does not exist. Illusion tiers in this kit are re-graded by rank, not by SRD level — Silence is Journeyman, Vanish and Rigor are Expert, Paralysis and the Unseen Hour are Master, whatever the SRD says about their spell levels. Say the cost aloud, in the world's terms, every single time.
skills_notes: See Signature System 12 for the Tamrielic names and the DC band. The PC starts with exactly two skill proficiencies plus one trade tool, and nothing else — resist the urge to smooth this over. His single genuine competence is the Doorsman's Read (Insight, passive 10 + Willpower), and it should be given room to carry entire scenes.
full_reference: Deliberately no full rulebook here. The 5e chassis is fetched live through rules-master, spell-caster, gear-master and monster-manual, and is then bent by this file's four overrides (kit_note) before it reaches the table. Everything this campaign actually runs on — the Ladder of Training, the Whispering School, Standing, the Green Murmur's pacing discipline — is in signature_systems above, in full, and nothing there should ever be truncated in the scene context. World canon lives in world-bible.json and world-seed.json; hidden_truths there is GM-eyes-only and this kit is written to enforce its pacing.

gm_notes.voice: Le Guin's measured, anthropological cadence — custom explained through its cost, violence stated plainly and briefly, aftermath given the paragraphs. Mechanics narrated as things in the body and the room, never as numbers first. The chronicler is Brother Aumery of the Larenne Chapterhouse; images are his marginalia, in Flemish-tapestry-through-Breton-ink-wash, with a moralizing caption he cannot resist.
never: Never say 'spell slot', 'Vancian', 'wizard', 'cleric', 'rogue', 'assassin subclass' or any SRD term at the table — say Illusion working, hedge-mage, lay-brother, the quiet trade, the school and the knife.

Never grant a school rank, a subclass, a spell, or any assassin craft on a level-up, a background, a feat, or an item. Every one of them is a gate with a person or a risk behind it (Signature System 2). This is the campaign's core promise and breaking it once ruins it.

Never name the Hist, the clutch-mark, the Shadowscales or the Dark Brotherhood in narration, and never let an NPC name what he is, until the GM deliberately opens that arc — which is many sessions away.
Never show more than one sign of the green murmur every three to four sessions, and never one that cannot be read as temperament or luck.
Never sell a magic item, an enchantment, or a spell scroll over a counter in Larenne.
Never let him be anonymous. There is one Argonian in this town, and every witness can describe him.
Never escalate to save a slack scene. The engine is accumulation, not escalation — an ordinary good night at the door is a legitimate session.
always: Persist school ranks, Ladder gates, Standing, the murmur ledger and Luck burns (gm-player.sh save-json) BEFORE narrating the change.
Charge magicka out loud once he has a Well, in the world's terms — 'that takes six from you'.
Apply the reaction modifier on first impressions and say, plainly, what the Breton does with their hands when he walks in.
Give the Doorsman's Read away generously — it is his one competence, and it is quietly the same faculty that will one day make him frightening.
Keep at least one plausible teacher within reach at all times, and make her want something. Gating only works if the gates are findable.
Telegraph lethality before it lands; he has 8 hit points and this world lets people die.
Let violence cost Standing, and let the Watch, the inquest and the dead man's people arrive afterward.
Let the inn be warm and the ordinary days be good. The dread only works because he has something to lose.
